rationale: Both round-6 asks are addressed: the reviewed_head_sha value classes handle the real 6ou2 'design-review-no-code' registration (skipped and reported), and a typed ErrPathNotAtRef probe tells an absent plan.md on spec/<S> apart from a git failure. The diff introduces no defect. The claims I re-derived (FindRoot, the bead -rN re-derivation giving zero, and the wellFormedGitObjectID class-(c) gate) hold. One non-blocking nit: cat-file -e exit 128 does not separate a gc'd object from a git failure, though both refuse.

findings.title: Round-6 ask status
findings.detail: Both are ADDRESSED at e7388f71. (1) 6ou2 placeholder: R4.2 F2 now has value classes (a) empty → skipped, (b) non-SHA placeholder → skipped and reported, (c) well-formed object ID → evaluated, (d) option-like or revision-expression → MALFORMED, fail closed. R4.3's set uses the same classes, and only (c) is ever a git operand. 'design-review-no-code' is class (b) because it has no leading '-' and no revision characters, and AC-11 (x-p) pins the exact 6ou2 shape. (2) Absent vs failed: a typed probe ('rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/spec/<S>', then 'ls-tree spec/<S> -- <path>', where empty output means absent and a non-zero exit means failure, then the blob read) is a new gitutil helper returning ErrPathNotAtRef. Only ref-absent or path-absent falls through to the checkout. The fifth fixture pins both the absent case and the probe-failure case.

findings.title: Regression check of 8b3a5535..e7388f71
findings.detail: No defect introduced. Verified: workspace.FindRoot exists (workspace.go:33). The documented re-derivation (bead_id non-null panel.json at 8b3a5535 whose dir matches -r[0-9]+$) yields zero matches, as stated. prerelease-r2 has bead_id null. wellFormedGitObjectID is the class-(c) gate. One nit, which does not block: 'git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}' exits 128 both for a missing object ('Not a valid object name') and for a genuine git failure. So 'a gc'd SHA is outside-tip, never an F5 error' can, in a broken repo, label an infra failure as UnlandedReview. Both outcomes refuse, so this is fail-closed and only the message class can be wrong. The plan can tell them apart by first checking that the repo is readable, for example with rev-parse of the spec tip, which the fallback already needs. A second nit: a hex string shorter than 7 characters is classed as a placeholder (skipped), not malformed. That is acceptable, because it cannot name a commit unambiguously.
